target_claim: The described crossing procedure (initial trip carrying the whole cover C, K two-trip cover-delivery rounds, then a final stage in which Charon returns empty or with one non-conflicting passenger to fetch the independent set L1) produces a valid crossing sequence in which the bank without Charon always holds an independent set. This is false: during the final stage the right bank holds the cover C (minus at most one carried passenger) unsupervised, and a vertex cover generally contains edges, so two enemies are left together without Charon.
source_quote:
This procedure produces a valid sequence of crossings using boat capacity k = K + 1.
At every point, the bank without Charon holds either an independent set of H’s vertices or
is empty.
test_sketch: Implement the schedule generator exactly as written (~100 lines): trip 1 carries C left->right; for i=1..K do Trip A (carry C\{ci} right->left) and Trip B (carry C\{ci} left->right); final stage: Charon returns empty (or with one passenger) and ferries up to K members of L1 per trip. Oracle: a simulator that after every trip checks that the bank without Charon induces no edge of H. Input family: H = complete graph K_m, K = m-1 (a valid vertex cover of size K exists), k = K+1, for m = 3 and 4. For H = K4, K = 3, C = {1,2,3}, L1 = {4}: every final-stage return trip allowed by the text leaves at least two mutually adjacent cover vertices unsupervised on the right bank; the checker flags a safety violation (for H = triangle the 'return empty' option already violates safety). A brute-force BFS over states (n <= 12) confirms a valid schedule does exist, so the failure is in their procedure, not the decision answer.
